Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS: The December 15, 2021 FOMC statement is constructive on growth and employment but flags elevated inflation and pandemic uncertainty. SLOOS around this period points to broadly more accommodative credit conditions that reinforce the constructive tone: banks eased standards across residential real estate (including HELOCs and jumbo), multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential CRE, and consumer credit (credit cards and autos), with increased credit limits and lower auto loan rates; many banks expected stronger demand for C&I and credit cards, and reported stronger consumer loan demand. Foreign banks also eased CRE standards and saw stronger CRE demand. Offsets include reports of weaker demand in some categories (auto and some C&I), unchanged standards for government residential mortgages, and unchanged demand for construction/land development. Balancing these SLOOS signals against the inflation and pandemic risks cited by the FOMC and stability concerns noted in the Financial Stability Report, the overall tone shifts modestly more positive than before but remains cautious.
